Let me analyze this OIML certificate for ultrasonic gas meters (R137-1).

Key facts:
- Certificate number: R137/2012-B-NL1-18.09 revision 1
- Scheme: B
- Project number: 1902613
- Page total: 4
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 30 August 2018
- OIML issuer ID: NL1
- Issuing authority: NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1
- Address: Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, the Netherlands
- Person responsible: C. Oosterman, Head Certification Board
- Phone: +31 78 6332332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl

Applicant and Manufacturer:
- Daniel Measurement and Control, Inc., 11100 Brittmoore Park Drive, 77041 Houston, Texas, United States of America
- Manufacturer's name: Daniel

Also there are two production locations: Daniel Measurement and Control (Houston) and Emerson SRL, Emerson street no. 4, 400461 Cluj-Napoca, Romania. Hmm, production locations — Emerson SRL is a production location, not necessarily manufacturer. The certificate says "Applicant and Manufacturer: Daniel Measurement and Control, Inc." I could add Emerson SRL as a manufacturer? Better to keep manufacturers as listed (Daniel), but maybe note production locations. The schema doesn't have production_locations. I could include manufacturers with both? The cert explicitly states the manufacturer is Daniel Measurement and Control. Production locations include Emerson SRL. Hmm — safest: manufacturers = [Daniel Measurement and Control, Inc.]. Maybe include Emerson SRL as manufacturer too since it's a production site... The schema says manufacturers[].name, address_lines[]. I'll keep just Daniel, but could add Emerson SRL as a second manufacturer entry since the cert mentions production there. Actually rule 8: don't fabricate. The document says "The ultrasonic gas meter is produced at the following production locations: Daniel... and Emerson SRL...". Being a production location doesn't make it a manufacturer per the cert's own labeling ("Applicant and Manufacturer: Daniel"). I'll keep Daniel only, and perhaps record production locations... there's no field. Maybe skip, or include Emerson SRL as manufacturer with a note? I'll add only Daniel to manufacturers. Hmm, but production locations might be useful. I could include both in manufacturers since "produced at" implies manufacturing. Risky. I'll include both, marking Emerson SRL — no, schema has no note field for manufacturers. I'll just include Daniel. Actually, let me reconsider: many extraction tasks would want production locations captured. I could put it in certificate description? certified_type.description is "free-text description if present". I could include a note there. The description: "An ultrasonic gas meter". I'll mention production locations in description? That may be over-reach but it's free-text description... The description field is for the certified type description. I'll keep it simple: "Ultrasonic gas meter". Maybe include type names.

Certified type:
- category: "Gas meter"
- type_designations: "3414 / 3415 / 3416 / 3417 GUSM or Senior Sonic". So types: "3414 GUSM", "3415 GUSM", "3416 GUSM", "3417 GUSM", and "Senior Sonic" variants? The type designation is "3414 / 3415 / 3416 / 3417 GUSM or Senior Sonic". I'd list type_designations: ["3414 GUSM", "3415 GUSM", "3416 GUSM", "3417 GUSM", "Senior Sonic"]. Hmm, or perhaps ["3414", "3415", "3416", "3417"] with family name "GUSM or Senior Sonic". The models in the family: 3414, 3415, 3416, 3417.

model_family:
- family_name: "GUSM or Senior Sonic"? Actually "GUSM or Senior Sonic" seems to be product line names. family_name: null? Could set "GUSM / Senior Sonic". I'll set family_name: "GUSM or Senior Sonic" — hmm, that's the type naming. Actually "Type: 3414 / 3415 / 3416 / 3417 GUSM or Senior Sonic" means types 3414/3415/3416/3417 under the GUSM or Senior Sonic product names. So family_name: "GUSM or Senior Sonic".

models: 3414, 3415, 3416, 3417 with labels describing path configurations:
- 3414: 4 measuring paths in horizontal configuration
- 3415: model 3414 path layout and electronics + one check path connected to separate electronics
- 3416: model 3414 path layout and electronics + one check path and one diagnostic path connected to separate electronics
- 3417: two model 3414 electronics and transducers built into a model 3417 spool piece; usable in two configurations (two separate gas meters; pay/check configuration)

Components: the models have check paths, diagnostic paths, transducers (T11, T12, T21, T22, T32, T41). Transducer types are sub-assemblies. I could add components for transducers with alternatives OR. The transducer table is a config_level characteristic: gas temperature range per transducer type. Axis: transducer_type. Values:
- T11: -20 to +55 °C
- T12: -20 to +55 °C
- T21: -20 to +55 °C
- T22: -40 to +55 °C
- T32: -40 to +55 °C
- T41: -50 to +100 °C

That's config_level: attribute "gas_temperature_range", axis "transducer_type", values with condition "T11" etc.

Table 1 general characteristics:
- destined_for_measurement: "Gas volume" — string value. Characteristic type_level: {value: "Gas volume", unit_symbol: null}. Canonical label: measured_medium? "destined_for_the_measurement_of" → maybe "measured_quantity". I'll use "destined_for_measurement" with value "Gas volume". Hmm, keep it as measured quantity. Let me use "destined_for_measurement": {"value": "Gas volume"}.

- environmental_classes: "M2 / E2" → value string "M2/E2"? These are two classes: humidity class M2 and environmental class E2. Could split into humidity_class: M2, environmental_class: E2. R137 defines classes: accuracy class, humidity class (M), mechanical environment... Actually for gas meters: M2 is humidity/magnetic? In OIML, "M2" is a mechanical environment class, "E2" climatic environment class. I'll record environmental_class_mechanical: "M2", environmental_class_climatic: "E2"? Simpler: environmental_classes: "M2 / E2" as string. I'll do environmental_classes: {value: "M2/E2"}. Hmm, splitting is nicer: mechanical_environment_class: "M2", climatic_environment_class: "E2". I'll do that? Risky interpretation. I'll keep environmental_classes as one string value.

- accuracy_class: 0.5 (0,5 → 0.5). type_level numeric.

- maximum_pressure: 425 bar.

- ambient_temperature_range: -40 to +55 °C → value {min: -40, max: 55}, unit "°C".

- designed_for: "Condensing humidity" → string.

- orientation: "All orientations" → string.

- power_supply_voltage: 10.4 – 36 V DC → value {min: 10.4, max: 36}, unit "V", plus power_supply_type: "DC".

- software_identification: versions with checksums. List of versions: 1.24/1869761847, 1.27/2717395331, 1.30/2620208593, 1.31/3367318398, 1.35/1438734832. How to record? Could be type_level with value as string, or config_level with axis "software_version". Better: characteristic "software_version" list... The schema value can be a string. I could create type_level entries: software_version_number with value as list? Schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. Multiple software versions — maybe config_level with axis "software_version": values [{condition: "1.24", value: 1869761847}, ...] with attribute "software_checksum". That's neat: attribute "software_checksum", axis "software_version", condition "1.24" → 1869761847, etc. I'll do that.

Table 2 — family of instruments by diameter (DN):
Columns: DN [mm], Typical range [mm], Vmin [m/s], Vt [m/s], Vmax [m/s].
Rows: DN 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450 → Vmax 30.5; DN 500 → 32.5; 600 → 30.5; 750 → 26; 900 → 23; 1050 → 21.
Vmin = 0.5 m/s (0,5 → 0.5) for all (rowspan 13).
Vt = 0.1 × Vmax for all (rowspan 13) → formula string "0.1 × Vmax" or "0.1*Vmax". Keep as string "0.1 x Vmax" — canonical: value "0.1 × Vmax". No LaTeX so fine. Use "0.1 x Vmax"? The markdown says "0,1 x Vmax". I'll use "0.1 x Vmax" with decimal fixed.

Model family models: here the variants are by DN size: DN100...DN1050 (13 sizes). Should model_family.models be the DN sizes? The models 3414-3417 × DN sizes. The family of instruments is characterized by diameter. I think model_family.models should be the type models 3414/3415/3416/3417, and the DN sizes become config axis "nominal_diameter" or matrix table. Alternatively models = DN sizes. Hmm.

The R137 example in the instructions had models G1.6, G2.5 from a size table — the sizes became models. But here we have explicit models 3414-3417 too. The characteristics vary by DN, not by model 3414-3417 (Table 2 is "general characteristics of the family of instruments" — applies across models).

I think best: model_family.models = 3414, 3415, 3416, 3417 (with labels describing configurations). The DN-dependent flow velocities go to matrix_tables and config_level with axis "nominal_diameter" (DN in mm).

config_level entries:
- attribute "maximum_velocity_vmax", axis "nominal_diameter_dn_mm", values: condition "DN100" → 30.5 m/s, ..., DN500 → 32.5, DN600 → 30.5, DN750 → 26, DN900 → 23, DN1050 → 21.
- attribute "minimum_velocity_vmin", axis same, all 0.5 m/s — constant, so could be type_level. Since constant across all, type_level: minimum_velocity: 0.5 m/s. And transition velocity vt: "0.1 x Vmax" formula — type_level as string with unit m/s.

matrix_tables: Table 2 with columns dn_mm, typical_range_mm (string "80 ~ 108"), vmin_mps, vt_mps, vmax_mps. Rows for each DN.

Should I also emit model_level for qmax-like attributes? The instruction example for R137 used size as model. But here DN is not the model; the models are 3414-3417. The varying attribute axis is DN — a configuration axis. I'll use config_level for vmax per DN, plus matrix_tables for the full table. That seems right per rule 5 (attributes vary by configuration → config_level).

Conditions: "DN100", "DN150", ..., "DN1050".

Typical range values: e.g. "80-108" mm — inner diameter range presumably. In matrix rows keep as string "80 ~ 108" or {min:80, max:108}. In matrix tables, rows are objects; I could use {"min": 80, "max": 108} or a string "80-108". For matrix table simplicity, string "80-108" is fine, but structured value is nicer. The matrix_tables rows aren't strictly bound to the structured value shape. I'll use strings "80-108".

Recommendation: R137-1 (2012). Canonical id "R137" (e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60"). id: "R137", edition: 2012? The example said edition (int). R137-1 (2012): id could be "R137-1" with edition 2012. Hmm — canonical might be "R137". The recommendation title "Gas meters", part 1. I'll use id "R137-1", edition 2012. Or id "R137", edition 2012, and note part 1? Schema: id, edition, amendment, scheme, accuracy_classes. I'll use id: "R137", edition: 2012, amendment: null... Actually "R137-1" is more precise. The rule says canonical e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60". For R137-1, I'd go with "R137". Hmm, but part 1 matters (R137-1 & -2 exist). I'll use "R137-1" — wait, but then edition 2012. Let me do id: "R137-1", edition: 2012. Actually, to be safe with canonicalization "R60 not OIML R 60", "R137-1" still fits the pattern. I'll go with "R137-1".

scheme: "B". accuracy_classes: [0.5].

test_reports:
- NMi-15200438-01, 3 November 2015, 47 pages, role test_report (or type_evaluation_report). The cert says "conformity was established by the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated report(s)". These are OIML Type Evaluation Reports. Role: type_evaluation_report seems apt for all. The doc mentions "OIML Type Evaluation Report". I'll set role "type_evaluation_report" for all five. Dates: 2015-11-03 (47 pages), 2016-02-25 (50 pages), 2016-08-19 (11 pages), 2016-11-03 (7 pages), 2018-08-23 (51 pages).

Documentation folder: T11159-2 — could be a test_reports entry with role "documentation_file": id "T11159-2". Yes: "The construction of the measuring instrument is recorded in Documentation folder number T11159-2." role: documentation_file.

Also document 11159/0-13 referenced in installation conditions (piping configuration doc) — minor; skip or include? It's a reference document. I'll skip; or include as documentation_file "11159/0-13"? It says "See document 11159/0-13". Probably skip to avoid noise. Hmm, it's part of installation conditions. I'll skip.

Installation conditions: config_level? "5D piping followed by CPA 50E/CPA 55E straightener followed by 10D piping at inlet". Could be a config_level characteristic: attribute "inlet_piping_configuration", axis "installation", value string "5D piping + CPA 50E/CPA 55E straightener + 10D piping". Or components entry for flow straightener: type_designations ["CPA 50E", "CPA 55E"], alternatives "OR". That's a named sub-assembly alternative — good components entry. I'll add component: role "flow_straightener", type_designations ["CPA 50E", "CPA 55E"], alternatives "OR". And config_level: attribute "inlet_piping", axis "straightener", conditions "with CPA 50E/CPA 55E straightener": value "5D upstream + 10D downstream... " Hmm. Keep it simpler: config_level entry attribute "minimum_inlet_piping_length", axis "flow_straightener", values [{condition: "CPA 50E or CPA 55E straightener", value: {min: 5, max: 10}? no...]. It's 5D before straightener and 10D after. Two values. Could do:
- attribute "upstream_piping_length", axis "installation_configuration", value 5, unit "D" (D = pipe diameter) condition "CPA 50E/CPA 55E straightener installed"
- attribute "downstream_piping_length"... wait, the 10D is between straightener and meter, still upstream of meter.

Simpler: one config_level: attribute "inlet_piping", axis "flow_straightener", values: [{condition: "CPA 50E / CPA 55E straightener", value: "5D piping + straightener + 10D piping", unit null}]. Value is a string formula-ish. Acceptable. I'll include it.

Model 3417 configurations: "Two separate gas meters" or "Pay/check configuration" — could be config_level: attribute "operating_configuration", axis "model 3417 usage", values [{condition: ..., value: "Two separate gas meters"}, {condition ..., value: "Pay / check configuration"}]. Hmm, that's more of a model attribute. I'll put it in the model label/attributes: model 3417 attributes {usage_configurations: ["Two separate gas meters", "Pay / check configuration"]}. models[].attributes{} is free-form. Good.

- T12 same, T21 same

Also ambient temperature -40/+55 (type_level).

Also maybe components for the meter body/paths? Not named. Skip.

Footnotes: none in the doc. Omit.

model_level: Should I add anything? The models 3414-3417 differ by path configuration which I captured in model labels/attributes. No numeric model-level matrix needed. But maybe I should include DN sizes as models too? The instruction example made sizes models for R137. But that example had no explicit model numbers. Here explicit models exist. I'll keep models 3414-3417, DN as config axis.

Hmm, but then model_level would be empty — fine, omit or empty. I could add model_level entries where attributes differ per model: e.g., check_path presence: 3415 has 1 check path, 3416 has 1 check path + 1 diagnostic path. Could do model_level:
- attribute "measuring_paths", values [{model: "3414", value: 4}, {3415: 4}, {3416: 4}, {3417: 8 (two 3414 electronics)?}]. 3417 is composed of two model 3414 electronics → 8 paths? "two model 3414 electronics and transducers built into a model 3417 spool piece" — so 2×4 = 8 measuring paths. That's inference; risky but reasonable. I'll keep it safer: attribute "number_of_measuring_paths": 3414: 4, 3415: 4, 3416: 4, 3417: 8. Hmm, 3417 "two model 3414 electronics" → yes 8. But I worry about fabrication. It's a direct composition statement; I'll include 8 with confidence. Alternatively put path info in model attributes strings only. Let me do model_level for number_of_measuring_paths: 4,4,4,8 — I think it's justified.

Also "check_paths": 3414: 0, 3415: 1, 3416: 1, 3417: 0? For 3417 in pay/check config... uncertain. Skip check_paths as model_level; keep in attributes.

Actually, let me put the path descriptions in models[].attributes as strings and also include model_level for number_of_measuring_paths. Fine.

certified_type.module_designation: for gas meters — "Not applicable"? The schema field is from load cell certs ("Analog load cell"). Gas meter → null or "Not applicable". I'll use null... The field definition: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For a complete measuring instrument (gas meter is the whole instrument), "Not applicable" seems right. I'll put "Not applicable".

description: "Ultrasonic gas meter, types 3414/3415/3416/3417 GUSM or Senior Sonic, for the measurement of gas volume, produced in the USA and Romania." Keep concise: "Ultrasonic gas meter". - environmental_classes: {"value": "M2/E2"} — hmm the doc says "M2 / E2". I'll record two separate? I'll do one: value "M2 / E2" → "M2/E2". Let me split into "humidity_class"? So mechanical_environment_class "M2", climatic_environment_class "E2". I'll split — it's accurate. Label: "environmental_class_mechanical": "M2", "environmental_class_climatic": "E2". Reasonable. software versions → config_level.

Now labels style: use canonical snake_case. Values with unit objects: {"value": ..., "unit_symbol": ..., "unit_id": null}. Note the schema in rule 2 shows unit_id inside each value object. The example uses "u:degree_Celsius" pattern. I'll set "u:degree_Celsius" for temperature ones. Others null.
